title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference: September 28, 2026
headline: No injuries reported, but LaFleur is frustrated with a lack of explosive plays and self-inflicted penalties, and he praised LB Jack Gibbens.
summary: LaFleur said the offense has been efficient for most of the season but needs more explosive plays. He attributed the lack of big gains to a mix of blocking details, receivers not getting connected, and checkdowns, rather than to any one player. He said the penalties, especially three pre-snap and post-snap penalties on the first three drives, were a team-wide problem that put the offense in a hole. On defense, he said the team's play style is right but it needs clarity and cleaner execution on blitz timing, fronts, and tackling. He called the run blocking better but still full of busts, and he took responsibility for them as a coaching issue. He said there were no injuries from the game. He praised Marvin Harrison Jr.'s route-running and said he is looking forward to working with him again on Wednesday. He is also pleased with special teams, though he wants more. He praised Gibbens as a strong addition to the defense. The next opponent is New York, and LaFleur said the focus is on his own team, with situational adjustments for the opposing quarterback.

signals.note: Praise from the head coach for a defender who is around the ball a lot could point to a bigger defensive role.

signals.note: The coach's comments are positive, but he is not signaling a specific target increase, so this is a watch item.
signals.quote: I thought he did some nice stuff

signals.claim: Explosive plays depend on the whole unit and on checking down when the defense takes away the deep shot.
signals.note: The offense's lack of big plays is a shared issue, so Brissett's raw production may stay limited until the unit improves.

topics.detail: LaFleur said the offense has been efficient but needs more big plays. He said the explosives must come organically, with better downfield connection, checkdowns that become big gains, and better ball placement.
He described the penalties as a team problem, with three costly penalties in the first three drives. He wants them cleaned up and said the players already know this.
He said the defense battles but needs better clarity, alignments, and execution, especially on blitz timing and tackling. He said blitz results have been poor and tackling needs improvement.
Run blocking took a step forward, but there were still many busts. LaFleur said he takes responsibility for those as a coaching issue.
He said special teams has looked sharp, but the standard requires further improvement.
The focus is on the team's own execution. Adjustments for New York's quarterback, Jameis, are situational, targeting third downs and the red zone.

title: Jesse Minter Discusses Big-Time Plays and Areas of Improvement From Week 3 Win
headline: Nnamdi Madubuike played his first game in over a year and the coach is happy with him; Zay Flowers is on a snap count (about 21 plays) but trending toward a bigger role.
summary: Minter said the team was excited to be home for a normal week after a close Week 3 win abroad, and he praised the travel staff. He said Nnamdi Madubuike handled his first game back in over a year well, that he was kept off a strict play count, and that he should improve as he gets more reps. On Zay Flowers, Minter said the team capped him around 20 to 25 snaps, he played 21, and he is coming out of the injury ready to push toward a full-time role. He said Ronnie Stanley's toe should be much better this week after a first start at left tackle that went well. Minter said the offense's penalties and the defense's missed tackles and inconsistency were the main areas to fix, and he took responsibility for the defensive standard. He praised Lamar Jackson's leadership and his calm handling of mid-game center changes. Nate Wiggins made several good plays after a penalty. Minter also said Travis Jones's hamstring issue is minor and he is fine.

title: Joe Brady Reflects On Bills Win And Performance Against The Chargers
headline: Bills' Ray Davis is set to get more backfield work as Ty Johnson returns, Greg Rousseau is playing with confidence, and Christian Benford's injury status is still unclear.
summary: Brady said the medical staff will evaluate the bumps and bruises over the next few days, and he is not concerned about Josh Allen's usual day-after soreness. He praised Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun for handling their reps in outside cornerback, saying the more reps they get, the better for the team, and that he will never be confident with a particular 11 on the field. On ball security, he said the team must be more intentional about how it goes to the ground and covers the ball, and that the turnovers were within its control. He defended the defense's third-down performance, but said the first and second down efforts drive third-down results, and he said the team has to clean up tackling in the open field. He said the defense improved in its run fits and gap discipline, and the goal-line plan is complex but the team is handling it. Brady said Ty Johnson's return brings a unique dynamic and gave him full trust, and he wants to get Ray Davis more touches going forward. He said the fourth-down decisions were aggressive and not hesitant, and he credited Keon Coleman for making plays even without the stat line. Finally, he credited Bradley Chubb's leadership for Greg Rousseau's confident play and said the outside linebacker rotation will continue to be managed to keep players fresh.

title: Dave Canales provides injury updates after Browns game
headline: Panthers' injury outlook is mixed: Jaycee Horn likely heads to IR with a significant quad injury, Devin Lloyd is expected back, and Bryce Young is expected to play Sunday night against Detroit despite an ankle issue.
summary: Canales said the team fought back in Cleveland and was comfortable in the late-game situation, but the defense could not get the final stop. He called Jaycee Horn's quad injury significant and said he would not give a timeline or say whether it's a tear until second and third opinions come back, likely by Wednesday. He acknowledged Horn would probably be placed on IR but said nothing is definitive yet. Akayleb Evans filled in well at cornerback, Chau Smith-Wade will step into the rotation, and the team may elevate Corey Thornton from the practice squad while looking for other options. Damien Lewis has an elbow issue that is being imaged, and Jalen Coker's injury is also being evaluated, with the bye week factored into decisions. Devin Lloyd is expected back this week, Nick Scott's rib is considered playable, and Xavier Legette is day-to-day with a knee issue. On offense, Canales praised the run game's fundamentals and Chuba Hubbard's downhill running, but said Tetairoa McMillan's low target count was partly the staff's responsibility after Denzel Ward shadowed him. Bryce Young was sore after taking a cleat to the ankle; Canales wants to check it further but expects him to play Sunday night against the Lions.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: September 28th, 2026
headline: Tyson Campbell was close to playing against Pittsburgh and Monken feels good about him for Thursday, while Denzel Boston's low target count is a fix the offense plans to address.
summary: Monken said he had not yet watched the Pittsburgh tape and that the offense is a work in progress, with the passing game still needing to be sharpened with Deshaun Watson and the receivers. He attributed the offensive line's false starts and cadence problems to a mix of coaching, communication, and execution, and said the issues need to be fixed quickly on a short week. On injuries, he reported no lingering effects for Watson from a fourth-quarter hit and said Tytus Howard has been playing through nicks and bruises. Tyson Campbell was close to going in the game, and Monken feels good about him for Thursday. Dawand Jones has worked at both tackle spots, mostly right tackle lately, and is ready to step in. Monken said the team will have a better read on post-game health over the next day or two, and he would have an update on the knee injury involving a player named Tyler later in the day. On Denzel Boston, he admitted the team can move him around more and stack plays to get him more targets, and called the low target count partly a byproduct of game flow and protection. He praised Quincy Williams for playing faster and more comfortable in the system, and credited Denzel Ward and Grant Delpit for their play. The team's next game is a Thursday night contest.

title: HC Sean Payton on WR Pat Bryant vs. Rams: ‘It’s good to see him come up [big] in a game like that’
headline: Sean Payton praised WR Pat Bryant's hands, contested catches, and run-after-catch ability after his Week 3 game vs. the Rams, a positive usage signal.
summary: Payton said he was glad to see Pat Bryant produce in a game like the Rams win, noting Bryant has strong hands away from his body and high-pointed the two-point conversion target. He credited quarterback Bo Nix for finding a throwing lane, and said Bryant's run-after-catch skill, which the staff saw throughout training camp, showed up in live action. On penalties, Payton said the season is long, he has not seen a call reversed, and his focus is on penalties the team controls, such as pre-snap and post-snap ones. He downplayed the importance of the gun-versus-under-center split so far, noting only about three short-yardage snaps this season, and said the team typically lines up under center in short yardage when it plans to run. On the slow start, he said he did not think urgency was the main issue, pointing to defensive success and a tale-of-two-halves game, and said the fix is cleaning up early-down efficiency and the details of the game plan. He said the Rams' heavy passing late was mostly a byproduct of trailing in the second half, not a planned approach. He also said Bryant's movement on the two-point play was natural rather than something the team practices.

signals.claim: Bryant showed well in the Rams game, with the coach highlighting his hands, contested catch, and yards after catch.
signals.note: Payton's public praise, along with a two-point conversion target, suggests Bryant's role in the passing game is real and worth monitoring for volume.
signals.quote: it's good to see him, um, come up in a game like that.

Payton disputed that a lack of urgency caused the slow start. He pointed to strong defensive play and said the fix is early-down efficiency and game-plan details.
Payton said Stafford's high attempt total came mainly from the Rams trailing late, not from a planned pass-heavy approach.

title: Campbell on individual performances
headline: Rakestraw is set for more outside-corner reps and Nowaske's role is growing, while Cade Mays is unlikely for Carolina and returns after the bye.
summary: Campbell praised the offense for efficiency in the Week 3 win over the Jets, highlighting Jared Goff's 78% completion rate, a 117-yard, 4.7-average run game, and no turnovers. He singled out the offensive line, including Christian Mahogany, Blake Miller, and Tate Ratledge, for setting the tone in protection and the run game. On defense he credited the front for disrupting the quarterback and stopping the run, but said the secondary lost too many one-on-one matchups and that penalties and catch-point problems showed up at bad times. He said Ennis Rakestraw showed up and will get more reps, possibly more outside corner snaps in place of Roger McCreary, and that Trevor Nowaske has earned a bigger defensive role through discipline and special teams play. Campbell said Alim McNeill was close to another sack and is on the uptick. On injuries, Cade Mays is trending well but is a tall order for this week, with the bye as the more realistic target. Thomas Harper's status is uncertain and he will be out for a stretch. Amon-Ra St. Brown had a minor issue that Campbell does not believe is serious. The team faces Carolina on Sunday night.

title: Matt LaFleur on Watson's performance vs. Falcons: 'I thought that was Christian's best game'
headline: Watson had his best game of the season per LaFleur, but the team is still struggling on the O-line, run game, and penalties, and Jayden Reed's timeline is unknown.
summary: LaFleur said the week was about a reset and fine-tuning, with the main emphasis on fundamentals across the board. He said the team has to execute at a higher level and that the offensive line must improve quickly, especially pass sets and passing off twists, which he admitted have been a struggle. He said the line's issues stem from both players not being on the same page and failing to stop the initial movement, and that some pressure situations are unavoidable against good defensive lines. He acknowledged the run game has lacked efficiency, but said the team has to keep committing to it, calling it body blows, and that the coaching staff must do better. On Reed, he had no update on how long he might be out or whether he'd go to IR. He said the team is still evaluating the two new veteran guards, with Tomlinson potentially helping right away, and said Aaron Banks is a week-to-week question for Sunday. He praised Christian Watson, saying Thursday was his best game, and said the team still has many penalties to clean up.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Offensive Adjustments After Texans at Colts | Full Q&A
headline: Texans are 0-3 and Ryans is 'hopeful' Nico Collins and Ed Ingram return this week, while Jadeveon Clowney remains week to week; Woody Marks and the running backs are praised.
summary: Ryans said the offense needs to move the ball better and avoid quick three-and-outs, with better execution and coaching. He praised the running backs, especially Woody Marks, for explosive, physical runs and said the offensive line is finishing blocks well, but he admitted the run game needs schematic changes. Without Nico Collins, the offense has still found explosives from Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, and Dalton Schultz. Ryans said play-calling is adjustable week to week and that OC Nick Kelly is willing to adapt, with communication and alerts at the line allowing C.J. Stroud to change plays based on defensive looks. He took responsibility for the late-game timeout and the fourth-and-one call, saying the team was not good enough in those spots and he must make better decisions. He praised C.J. Stroud's maturity and leadership, and said the special teams blocking improved. He said Collins and Ed Ingram are hopeful to return this week, while Clowney is still week to week.

title: Andy Reid on Week 3 Matchup: 'Wins Are Very Hard To Get In This League' | Press Conference 9/28
headline: Rashee Rice's physical, yards-after-catch role is trending up, Chamarri Conner has a good chance to play, and Xavier Worthy's shoulder is improving; Kansas City visits the Raiders next, both teams 3-0.
summary: Andy Reid opened by calling the win over Miami hard-earned, praising the young Dolphins staff, and saying there were things to correct. He said the team came out of the game largely healthy. On the offense, he said Miami's focus on Kenneth Walker's run game shortened the game to about 40-something plays, but the team still produced in both the run and pass games and found bigger plays downfield. Reid praised Rashee Rice's physicality after the catch and described him as almost a running back playing receiver. Chamarri Conner practiced last week and will work again this week, and Reid said there is a good chance he plays. Xavier Worthy is still managing a shoulder issue that Reid says improves every week. Reid would not commit on Josh Simmons' return, saying he would announce it when it happened. Defensively, Reid said the team must tighten up its pass rush and third-down efforts, and that the second half was better. On Patrick Mahomes' hit, Reid said he got up and kept playing, and he described the roughing-the-passer calls as part of how the league protects quarterbacks. Reid said he expects a loud atmosphere for the Raiders rivalry game.

title: Sean McVay, Trent McDuffie & Kyren Williams discuss takeaways from Week 3 vs. the Broncos, building a resilient culture & more
headline: Puka Nacua is optimistic for Week 4 vs. the Eagles, Terrance Ferguson and Jaylen Watson are expected out, and Kyren Williams is a clear featured back.
summary: McVay opened by apologizing for a mix-up that cut short reporter questions after the loss, then gave an injury update: Colby Parkinson had no setback with his knee but has a shoulder issue, Terrance Ferguson has a medial ankle sprain, and Jaylen Watson dislocated his shoulder. He said Watson will not go on IR but will probably miss this week. On Puka Nacua, McVay said the team is optimistic he can play against Philadelphia because he is progressing, and that he had a good workout before the game. He said Myles Garrett is making good progress and that no timeline has been set. McVay acknowledged offensive mistakes, including self-inflicted penalties, a missed play call on an early second-half sequence, and stalled drives that left points on the board, and he took responsibility for those calls. He called Kyren Williams a stud, praised his all-around work as a runner, receiver and blocker, and said he wants to keep him a focal point going forward while still trusting Blake Corum as the hot hand. He also said he was pleased with Emmanuel Forbes replacing Watson, that the field-goal operation was excellent, and that the league had not yet responded to the Josh Wallace pass-interference review.

title: Kevin O'Connell Talks About The Trade of J.J. McCarthy, Justin Jefferson's Ankle, Win Over Tampa Bay
headline: Justin Jefferson has an ankle sprain that is not expected to be long-term but is still week-to-week; Josh Oliver is out after tearing a bicep, shifting more load to T.J. Hockenson.
summary: O'Connell opened by discussing the trade of J.J. McCarthy to the Giants, saying he had an emotional one-on-one with McCarthy and that the decision was made in the best interest of the organization. He credited GM Nolan (Nolan Mitchell is not on the roster, so the name is unverified) for handling the situation and said he remains confident in the quarterback room of Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz and Max Bredeson. Much of the Q&A focused on whether the team gave McCarthy enough development time, and O'Connell said the organization did everything it could, while admitting he would reflect on decisions such as the first preseason game. On the injury front, he said Josh Oliver has a torn bicep that requires surgery, and the tight end group as a whole will have to fill the gap, with T.J. Hockenson the most prominent name. Jefferson has an ankle sprain that avoids a long-term injury; the plan is to manage swelling and see how much of the week he can work. A receiver (transcribed as 'Chuck Demmings', name unverified) has a hamstring strain that is not considered significant but will likely cost him some time. O'Connell also said Kyler Murray lost time after only 11 plays in a game, and the offense needs to coach and play better. The team is 3-0 with a home game next at U.S. Bank Stadium.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 9/28: "The answers are here, they are in this building"
headline: Vrabel says Drake Maye has no lingering shoulder issue, but is working on his confidence; Ben Brown is back healthy and Greg Van Roten's status is still unclear.
summary: Vrabel said he knows of no lingering shoulder problem for Drake Maye from the Denver game. Maye was not on the injury report and had no treatment beyond normal warm-up maintenance, and Vrabel doesn't expect it to be an issue. On the Jacksonville loss, he said the team has to review what went wrong, keep the positives, and then move on. He listed the positives as some good offensive plays, improving pass protection, and special teams and defensive efforts like a tipped pass and an interception. He named the negatives as turnovers, failing to force turnovers, red-zone execution, a missed field goal, and a poor sideline kick return. On Maye, he said confidence comes from preparation and can't be manufactured, and he compared pressing too hard to gripping a golf club too tightly. Ben Brown is back healthy and was expected to start at center and first left guard, while Walter Rouse made some mistakes but competed. Greg Van Roten will be re-evaluated after more tests. Vrabel also said the team may adjust its practice schedule this week, with reduced-tempo reps and a red-zone session Friday.

title: Coach John Harbaugh on J.J. McCarthy trade, Brian Burns injury
headline: Jameis Winston remains the starter for Sunday vs. Arizona despite the McCarthy trade, while Brian Burns is headed for surgery after tearing his ACL.
summary: Harbaugh said the team acquired J.J. McCarthy after a quarterback need emerged when the previous starter got hurt, and he called McCarthy a talented, high-draft-pick quarterback with NFL experience who will make the team better. McCarthy will need a crash course on the offense, with extra work and game-by-game installs, though coaches have some familiarity with his Minnesota system. Harbaugh was firm that Jameis Winston is the starter for Sunday's game against the Cardinals and beyond, and that McCarthy will be either the No. 2 or No. 3 quarterback. On Brian Burns, Harbaugh confirmed an ACL tear that will require surgery, calling him the leader of the defense and a major loss. Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux are expected to take on bigger roles, with Carter already playing a lot and Thibodeaux set to play more snaps. Harbaugh said the pass rush has been stymied by quick throws, chipping and other schemes, and the staff needs to find new ways to get to the quarterback. He also said the team's front office and scouts liked McCarthy a lot before the draft, and he did not rule out a free-agent quarterback workout.

title: HC Aaron Glenn Press Conference (9/28) | Week 4
headline: Geno Smith praised after a 31-of-37 game, Garrett Wilson cleared from his head injury, and the run game needs fixing before Chicago; injury updates on several players come Wednesday.
summary: Glenn opened by saying he'll give a cleaner injury update Wednesday, with two players he'll specifically address. He said Garrett Wilson has been cleared from his head injury. He called the Week 3 loss a mix of positives on both sides of the ball and some special teams issues, and said the team needs urgency to fix them before facing Chicago, whose coach he knows well. He attributed the blitz breakdown to miscommunication along the offensive line plus Geno Smith needing to hold onto the ball. He said the run game slipped the last two weeks and that the passing game has developed a play style that has to be reconciled with it. On special teams, he acknowledged missing two key players and said depth players were promoted, with coverage units needing sharper concept execution. He praised Smith's processing, drops, and ball delivery under heavy pressure, while noting areas still to improve. On injuries, he is leaning on medical staff for return-to-play decisions for players who missed the game, including Minkah Fitzpatrick. He called the comeback from 14 down a sign of resilience and pointed to a fourth-down stop. On D'Angelo Ponds, he said he's improving, plays both nickel and outside corner, and that playing time must be earned.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Recaps Sunday's Loss, Looks Ahead To Week 4
headline: Julian Love is day-to-day at safety, Zach Charbonnet's return to practice is still undecided, and Trevon Diggs is close to returning from a long layoff.
summary: Macdonald said the tape brought mixed emotions: real flashes of the team he wants, plus shortfalls that need urgent fixing, with the offense's struggles against Washington's defense a particular concern. He credited Washington but said the Seahawks have plenty of room to grow in execution and in finding solutions during games. He said the second half forced them to throw more than he wanted, and the goal is to control games earlier so the run game can be used on their terms. He called special teams inconsistency "not good enough" and said no player is exempt from special teams consideration. On injuries, Julian Love is day-to-day after extensive work that went well this morning, and Charbonnet has no update yet on whether he will begin practicing this week, with a decision expected by Tuesday. Diggs is part of the conversation for playing time, has practiced well since arriving, and would be ready if the situation called for it. He defended Josh Jones against a tough matchup, saying he played hard and technically sound, and that the team will keep putting him in one-on-one situations. He praised Jaxon Smith-Njigba's blocking and said he needs to block better at the third level to help the run game. He said the team will keep weighing how often Nick Emmanwori plays because his placement affects three position groups, and he praised Emmanwori's effort. On the fumble, he said the team will keep giving Jadarian Price the ball, trusting him, while focusing on fundamentals.

summary: Bowles said Mayfield's injury is a dislocation with no ligament or tendon damage, and the minimum timeline is three weeks. Tampa Bay will keep Mayfield on the roster for now rather than place him on IR, and the timeline could come sooner than expected. Daniels will start, and the team may add a veteran or practice-squad quarterback for the stretch. Bowles said the offense was hurt by penalties, too many third-and-long situations, and a lack of blocking and coaching, calling it a combination of problems rather than one issue. He said Bucky Irving is not on the injury report, and that Jalen McMillan is awaiting an MRI result. Bowles praised Christian Rozeboom and a fill-in player for their play while Josiah Trotter is out, and said it is too early to know if Trotter or Rueben Bain could play this week. On the defense, he said it did enough to win in some ways but needs more takeaways and to avoid big plays. He attributed a long kick return to poor coverage alignment.

A big kick return was blamed on bad coverage alignment, with too many players in the same spot.
Bowles said the team is frustrated at 0-3 and believes its character is strong, but it must cut mistakes, especially penalties, and play with confidence rather than pressing.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 09/29/26
headline: Marcus Mariota is running the offense with Jayden Daniels still in a return-to-play process; Rachaad White, Samuel Cosmi, and Nick Cross are all still uncertain for the coming week.
summary: Quinn opened with an update on Leo Chenal, who had surgery that morning that went well, and said the team is encouraged by the reports. He said Jayden Daniels, Frankie Luvu, and Chig Okonkwo should all return to practice in some form this week. Daniels is working through a structured return-to-play process, with a lighter Wednesday and the bigger ramp-up coming Thursday, and a full-go decision is not yet made. Samuel Cosmi's travel status depends on further testing, with an update expected Tuesday. Quinn praised Mariota and Terry McLaurin for their in-game play, and said Mariota and the offense were in sync at the line with audibles. He also said Rachaad White showed toughness finishing the game despite a shoulder injury, and that Thursday and Friday will be his biggest test. On Lucas Patrick, Quinn said the new interior lineman was tough through a foot injury and the team wanted to keep balance in the run game. Austin Ekeler is expected to travel and will be integrated into a new offensive system over the next few days. Quinn said there is no update yet on Nick Cross's ability to travel to London or practice.

topics.detail: Quinn said the tackling was better in the first half, though there were still missed tackles on a big play. He said he liked the team's aggressiveness and takeaway chances and saw clear improvement in back-end communication.

Quinn said the team finally created turnovers by being intentional about tipped balls and fumble recoveries, and that the three turnovers led to scores. He also addressed three penalties from the last game and said a celebration penalty involving a player not in uniform was a discipline issue to fix.
Quinn said the team felt like it won as one group across all three phases and credited the competitive good-on-good practices three times a week for the performance.
